hook_text: Your sketch looks great. Nobody can build from it. Three square-on views fix that.
clip_script: A sketch shows the idea. A working drawing gives every size. Look at the machine square-on from the front, from the top, from the side. Flat, no perspective, so you can measure. First angle: front in the middle, top view below it, side view to the right. Scale 1 to 10: 1200 becomes 120 on paper, but you write 1200 on the dimension, the true size. Dashed lines for what is hidden. Centre lines for the drum and pulley. Each size once, where it is clearest. Parts list with numbers and balloons. Then ask: could a stranger build it? That is the test.
visual_style: Whiteboard A3 with a border and title block; three views appearing in first angle positions with projection lines; a dashed hidden line; a dimension 1200 appearing over a short drawn line; a parts list table.
mood: Precise and reassuring, like a drawing office.
pacing: Sketch versus drawing, three views, positions, scale, true size, dashed, once each, parts list, the test.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the front, top and side of a matchbox at 2 to 1.
